title: ZPA legacy endpoint wiring: shared paths, schedules, user codes and step-up levels
aliases: application endpoint shared by segment types

prose.text: The ZPA endpoint inventory is generated; this subject keeps only the places where a route is shared, renamed or wired differently by the sources. The base paths are in [[zpa.api.base-paths]].

prose.label: User codes.
prose.text: {{usercodes-go-path}} The two SDKs build the path differently {{divergence:usercodes-path}}.

prose.label: Step-up levels.
prose.text: The response shape differs by SDK [[zpa.api.policy-wire:step-up-auth-shape]]. {{stepup-no-writes}} {{stepup-sdk-read-only}} Whether the API has write verbs is open {{gap:stepup-write-verbs}}.

prose.label: Provisioning key types.
prose.text: The key association types are broader than the two the old inventory listed: [[zpa.sdk-go.service-defects:provider-provisioning-key-schema-and-importer]] and [[zpa.app-connectors.provisioning-key-tooling:python-key-types]].

checks.do: Which SDK built a user-code request, since the Go and Python paths differ by an associationType segment.
Whether a schedule call used /connectorSchedule, the only path the Go service wires and the one the OpenAPI document shows.

application-shared-path.statement: The Go SDK's standard, Browser Access, Inspection and PRA application segment services, and its by-type service, all use the same /application endpoint, with getAppsByType as a sub-route.

connector-schedule-wired.statement: The Go App Connector schedule service builds its path from /connectorSchedule, and the Python module uses /connectorSchedule too; the appconnectorcontroller package declares an /assistantSchedule constant that the schedule service does not use.

evidence.note: the schedule package declares its own scheduleEndpoint and does not import appconnectorcontroller

schedule-openapi.statement: The OpenAPI document has GET and POST on /connectorSchedule and on /serviceEdgeSchedule, and a PUT only on /serviceEdgeSchedule/{id}.

expect.operationId: Get a Configured App Connector schedule frequency.

evidence.note: PUT is the only operation on serviceEdgeSchedule/{id}

usercodes-go-path.statement: The Go SDK posts user codes to {customerId}/{associationType}/usercodes and {customerId}/{associationType}/usercodes/status with the association type as a bare path segment.

quotes: resp, err := service.Client.NewRequestDo(ctx, "POST", relativeURL, common.Filter{MicroTenantID: service.MicroTenantID()}, request, &v)
resp, err := service.Client.NewRequestDo(ctx, "POST", relativeURL, common.Filter{MicroTenantID: service.MicroTenantID()}, requestBody, &v)

stepup-sdk-read-only.statement: Neither SDK has a create, update or delete call for step-up auth levels.
stepup-sdk-read-only.conditions: Rests on reading the whole of each at the pin: step_up_auth.go is the Go package's only file and GetStepupAuthLevel its only func; the Python module defines only __init__ and get_step_up_auth_levels. A quote cannot pin the absence.

stepup-no-writes.statement: The Go step_up_auth service's `GetStepupAuthLevel` and the Python stepup_auth_level module's `get_step_up_auth_levels` read the /stepupauthlevel path, and the OpenAPI document has no route at that path.

evidence.note: step_up_auth.go is the package's only file and GetStepupAuthLevel its only func
the module's complete method list: __init__ and one read

usercodes-path.summary: The Go SDK and the Python SDK build the user-code verification path differently.

positions.says: Go puts the association type directly after the customer ID.
Python puts a literal associationType segment before the type.

usercodes-path.impact: One of the two paths is wrong or the API accepts both; the OpenAPI document has neither route, so user-code enrollment through a raw call needs a tenant test.

assistant-schedule-served.title: Whether the legacy API still serves /assistantSchedule
assistant-schedule-served.detail: Unverified legacy statement: whether the legacy API still serves /assistantSchedule or it is a retired alias of /connectorSchedule. The Go appconnectorcontroller package declares the constant without using it, and the Python module and the OpenAPI document use /connectorSchedule.
assistant-schedule-served.blocks: choosing the connector schedule path in raw calls

stepup-write-verbs.title: Whether the step-up authentication levels route accepts writes
stepup-write-verbs.detail: Unverified legacy statement: whether the API supports create, update or delete on /stepupauthlevel. Both SDKs expose only the read, and the OpenAPI document lacks the route.
